checks.invariant: Total memory retained by Archive::new is bounded by len(RESOURCE.001) regardless of how many RESOURCE.MAP entries alias it.
checks.result: Not enforced: bytes() checks each entry only against the volume; data.to_vec() per entry (resource.rs:31); no overlap rejection or aggregate cap; count <= 65535. Same-name entries overwrite (old copy freed), so amplification needs distinct names at overlapping offsets — not prevented by source; no fixture built.

checks.invariant: decompress terminates, cost linear in declared output (<= 16 MiB), no panic/OOB.
checks.result: Claimed holds: size checked before allocation; rle advances p each iteration; lzw new > free breaks, prefix[free] = old with old <= free-1 within an epoch so chains are acyclic (depth <= 4096); entry 256 after reset never traversed; first code > 255 walks zero-initialised slots; indexes < 4096.

checks.invariant: Ttm::parse terminates and does not panic on arbitrary TT3 bytes.
checks.result: Holds: p advances >= 2 per iteration; nargs > 6 or truncated args error; string slice bounded; frames never empty at last_mut().unwrap().

checks.invariant: No reachable OOB index/slice/overflow in chunks/bmp/scr/palette/ttm/ads/unpack_4bpp; image allocations bounded.
checks.result: Holds: header reads via bytes()/u16_at/u32_at (checked_add + get); chunk bodies bounded; palette uses get().unwrap_or(0); ads checks res.get(p+2..); unpack_4bpp caps first_nibble+count at 32M nibbles (saturating_add), so per-BMP pixels <= 32 MiB; scr w*h capped the same way.

candidates.title: Overlapping RESOURCE.MAP entries make Archive::new copy the volume many times
candidates.description: Archive::new bounds-checks each RESOURCE.MAP entry only against RESOURCE.001 and copies it with to_vec(); with up to 65535 entries and no overlap rejection or aggregate cap, retained memory can scale to about count x len(volume) at startup, including unattended .scr launches. SECURITY.md lists excessive memory use from malformed RESOURCE files as in scope.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: No aggregate bound on bytes copied and no non-overlap check in Archive::new (resource.rs:21-31); retained memory scales with entry count x entry size rather than len(RESOURCE.001).

trace.description: RESOURCE.MAP and RESOURCE.001 are read whole from the data directory with no size cap.
count is a u16 from the map; each entry's offset comes from the map and its size from the volume header at that offset.
data.to_vec() allocates a fresh copy of each in-bounds range; every distinct name is kept in the HashMap.

evidence.description: bytes() checks only start+len within the slice; it cannot see overlap with other entries.
Each entry's data range is validated alone against the volume.
An owned copy is inserted per distinct name, with no running total or cap such as MAX_UNPACKED.

blockers: No bounded local fixture was built; whether a crafted volume yields enough distinct names at overlapping offsets with large decoded sizes has been argued from source but not observed, so the retained-memory growth curve is unmeasured.

validation_plan.local: In the run sandbox (2 GiB address-space limit), link the harness rlib and call Archive::new on a small synthetic map/volume pair whose entries point to overlapping ranges with distinct names; record retained memory (peak RSS or allocation failure) at 2-3 small entry counts and show growth with count x size rather than volume length; stop at the first allocation failure.

hardening: Add an aggregate cap on total archive bytes in Archive::new (e.g. sum of sizes <= len(volume)), or store (offset, len) ranges into one shared volume buffer instead of to_vec() per entry.

Ttm::parse expands each 2-byte opcode into an Op of about 40 bytes plus a Vec per 0x0FF0 opcode, so a 16 MiB decompressed TT3 can reach several hundred MiB before frames.truncate(pages); consider capping ops/frames or truncating to pages while parsing.
lzw writes dictionary entry 256 from a stale previous-epoch old after a reset; skipping the insert for the first code after a reset would match standard LZW semantics.
read_ci uses fs::read with no size limit on RESOURCE.001/MAP; a file-size ceiling would bound startup memory.
